variables: [{"symbol": "A", "meaning": "nondimensional observation matrix", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "W", "meaning": "noise weight matrix after whitening", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "tensor"}, {"symbol": "L", "meaning": "regularization operator", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "lambda", "meaning": "regularization strength in declared scaled coordinates", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "coupling"}, {"symbol": "x_lambda", "meaning": "scaled unknown estimate", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "state"}, {"symbol": "b", "meaning": "scaled data", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "vector"}]
conditions: ["Finite linearized inverse model with consistent nondimensionalization; W positive; combined operator invertible on constrained unknowns."]
derivation: ["Minimize weighted data residual squared plus lambda times penalty squared.", "Set its derivative to zero to obtain normal equations."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "A=[1,1],b=1,L=identity", "steps": ["A*(1,−1)=0 proves a one-dimensional kernel.", "Minimum-norm solution chooses equal entries."], "result": "x=(1/2,1/2) is a prior-selected representative, not unique recovery from data.", "units": "dimensionless"}
limitingCases: ["As lambda→0 a unique well-conditioned full-rank inverse is recovered when it exists."]
pitfalls: ["A small residual, positive returned singular values of a rectangular matrix, or a plausible image does not remove an unobserved kernel."]

title: Covariance-aware uncertainty propagation
plain: A derived result inherits covariance as well as individual input uncertainties.
variables: [{"symbol": "y", "meaning": "scalar measurand g(x)", "unit": "declared output SI unit", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "x_i", "meaning": "input quantities with separately stated units", "unit": "declared input SI units", "kind": "state"}, {"symbol": "J", "meaning": "local sensitivity row", "unit": "output-unit/input-unit", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "Sigma", "meaning": "input covariance matrix", "unit": "input-unit products", "kind": "tensor"}, {"symbol": "u_c", "meaning": "combined standard uncertainty", "unit": "output SI unit", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Differentiable local measurement model and small enough uncertainties for first-order propagation; coverage probabilities require additional distributional/effective-DOF assumptions."]
derivation: ["Linearize delta y≈sum(Ji*delta xi).", "Take its variance, retaining cross terms."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "C=Q/V;Q,V have equal1% relative standard uncertainty", "steps": ["For independent errors, add squared sensitivities.", "For perfectly common fractional calibration error the correlated terms cancel."], "result": "Independent relative uC≈1.414%; common multiplicative error can cancel exactly in the ratio.", "units": "F or relative dimensionless"}
limitingCases: ["A zero sensitivity suppresses the corresponding first-order contribution, not necessarily higher-order error."]
pitfalls: ["Multiplying by k=2 is not automatically a valid95% interval, and a nonsignificant difference is not equivalence."]

title: Magnetic flux continuity
plain: Divergence-free B has zero net outward flux through a closed surface.
variables: [{"symbol": "B", "meaning": "magnetic flux density", "unit": "T", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "V", "meaning": "enclosed region", "unit": "m^3", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "da", "meaning": "oriented outward area element", "unit": "m^2", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "nabla", "meaning": "spatial derivative", "unit": "1/m", "kind": "operator"}]
conditions: ["Classical Maxwell theory with no magnetic monopoles; include all faces of a closed surface."]
derivation: ["Apply the divergence theorem to local flux continuity.", "Opposite face contributions cancel for a uniform field."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "Bz=0.01 T; cube side=0.1 m", "steps": ["Top flux=+0.0001 Wb; bottom=-0.0001 Wb; sides zero."], "result": "Net flux=0", "units": "Wb"}
limitingCases: ["A nonzero open-surface flux is entirely compatible."]
pitfalls: ["Zero divergence does not imply zero curl or zero local field."]

title: Biot–Savart law for a filament
latex: \mathbf B(\mathbf r)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int \frac{d\boldsymbol\ell\times(\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime)}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime|^3}
plain: Sum oriented steady-current elements using the inverse-distance vector kernel.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "I", "meaning": "steady line current", "unit": "A", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "r", "meaning": "observation point", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "rprime", "meaning": "source point", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "dl", "meaning": "oriented line element in current direction", "unit": "m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "resulting flux density", "unit": "T", "kind": "vector"}]
conditions: ["Steady localized current with a physically completed return path; vacuum.", "Observation point is outside the ideal filament."]
derivation: ["Solve the vector Poisson equation in Coulomb gauge with the free-space Green function.", "Take its curl to obtain the cross-product kernel."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "Circular loop I=1 A, R=0.1 m; evaluate centre", "steps": ["All axial contributions add; transverse contributions cancel.", "Integrate circumference to obtain mu0 I/(2R)."], "result": "B=6.2831853 microtesla", "units": "T"}
limitingCases: ["The far field of a localized closed loop is dipolar, not an isolated-wire 1/r field."]
pitfalls: ["Do not omit return current when predicting a finite device field."]

title: Infinite straight wire
plain: Cylindrical symmetry turns Ampere circulation into an azimuthal field.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "I", "meaning": "wire current", "unit": "A", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "r", "meaning": "distance from wire axis", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "Bphi", "meaning": "azimuthal flux density, right-hand sense", "unit": "T", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Infinite thin wire, vacuum, stationary current; r exceeds conductor radius."]
derivation: ["Choose a coaxial circular contour.", "B is tangential and constant on the contour, so 2 pi r B=mu0 I."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "I=2 A; r=0.05 m", "steps": ["Substitute into mu0*2/(2*pi*0.05)."], "result": "B=8.0 microtesla", "units": "T"}
limitingCases: ["As I tends to zero, B vanishes; the singular r→0 limit is outside the thin-wire domain."]
pitfalls: ["A finite wire cannot inherit this expression arbitrarily close to its ends."]

title: On-axis circular-loop field
plain: The axial field of a thin circular loop interpolates between centre field and a dipole.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "I", "meaning": "oriented loop current", "unit": "A", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "R", "meaning": "loop radius", "unit": "m", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "z", "meaning": "distance along oriented loop axis", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "Bz", "meaning": "axial flux density", "unit": "T", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Circular filament in vacuum; observation on its symmetry axis."]
derivation: ["Project the Biot–Savart cross product onto the axis.", "The denominator is constant around the loop; integrate azimuth."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "I=1 A; R=0.1 m; z=0.1 m", "steps": ["Centre field=6.283 microtesla.", "Multiply by (1+1)^(-3/2)."], "result": "Bz=2.22144 microtesla", "units": "T"}
limitingCases: ["At z=0 recover mu0 I/(2R); for |z|≫R recover z^-3."]
pitfalls: ["The expression is not the off-axis field of a finite solenoid."]

title: Magnetostatic free-current circulation
plain: H circulation counts free current after magnetization is separated out.
variables: [{"symbol": "H", "meaning": "magnetic field intensity", "unit": "A/m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "Jf", "meaning": "free-current density", "unit": "A/m^2", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "C", "meaning": "oriented closed contour", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "dl", "meaning": "oriented line increment", "unit": "m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "Ifenc", "meaning": "free current through compatible surface", "unit": "A", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Stationary fields; displacement current negligible; contour and normal follow right-hand orientation."]
derivation: ["Apply Stokes theorem to curl H=Jf.", "Integrate current density over the spanning surface."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "Ienc=3 A; circular contour radius=0.1 m with cylindrical symmetry", "steps": ["H is constant and tangential.", "Divide 3 A by 2*pi*0.1 m."], "result": "H=4.77465 A/m", "units": "A/m"}
limitingCases: ["Zero enclosed current gives zero circulation, not necessarily H=0 everywhere."]
pitfalls: ["Ampere law does not justify constant H on a nonsymmetric contour."]

title: Long-solenoid interior estimate
plain: Turns per unit length set the ideal long air-core coil field.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "n", "meaning": "turn density", "unit": "1/m", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "I", "meaning": "coil current", "unit": "A", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "interior axial field", "unit": "T", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Length much larger than radius, observation away from ends, air core, negligible winding thickness."]
derivation: ["Choose an Ampere rectangle along the interior and remote exterior.", "Neglect exterior contribution and count n*l turns."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "n=1000/m; I=0.1 A", "steps": ["Compute mu0*100 A/m."], "result": "B≈0.125664 mT", "units": "T"}
limitingCases: ["At an ideal long coil end the on-axis field is about half the deep-interior value."]
pitfalls: ["Real coil heating, fringe fields and magnetic core saturation are separate calculations."]

title: Macroscopic B–H–M relation
plain: Magnetization is magnetic moment per material volume; the relation defines H in SI.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "magnetic induction", "unit": "T", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "H", "meaning": "field intensity", "unit": "A/m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "M", "meaning": "magnetization", "unit": "A/m", "kind": "vector"}]
conditions: ["Macroscopic SI fields defined at compatible coarse-graining scale."]
derivation: ["Separate microscopic current into free and magnetization contributions.", "Define H=B/mu0−M; no linear material law is assumed."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "Collinear H=100 A/m and M=900 A/m", "steps": ["Sum H+M=1000 A/m."], "result": "B=1.256637 mT", "units": "T"}
limitingCases: ["For M=0, vacuum B=mu0 H; at H=0 an ordered sample can have M≠0."]
pitfalls: ["B and H do not have the same SI units; B=mu H additionally assumes a constitutive law."]

title: Volume magnetization current
plain: Spatially varying magnetization has an equivalent bound volume current.
variables: [{"symbol": "Jb", "meaning": "bound volume current density", "unit": "A/m^2", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "M", "meaning": "magnetization", "unit": "A/m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "nabla", "meaning": "spatial derivative", "unit": "1/m", "kind": "operator"}]
conditions: ["Continuum magnetization differentiable inside the material; add interface surface currents separately."]
derivation: ["Represent localized magnetic moments as small current loops.", "Interior loop contributions cancel except where magnetization varies."]
workedExample: {"inputs": "M=(0,0,a*x), a=1000 A/m^2", "steps": ["Curl gives Jb_y=−dMz/dx."], "result": "Jb=(0,−1000,0) A/m²", "units": "A/m^2"}
limitingCases: ["Uniform M has zero volume curl but generally nonzero surface current."]
pitfalls: ["Zero Jb in the bulk does not imply an unmagnetized body."]

title: Surface magnetization current
plain: The boundary current closes magnetization loops at an interface.
variables: [{"symbol": "Kb", "meaning": "bound surface current density", "unit": "A/m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "M", "meaning": "magnetization inside relative to outside", "unit": "A/m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "n", "meaning": "outward unit surface normal", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "vector"}]
conditions: ["Use the magnetization jump if both sides are magnetic; orientation is outward from the chosen body."]

workedExample: {"inputs": "M=1000 zhat A/m; surface normal=xhat", "steps": ["zhat cross xhat = yhat."], "result": "Kb=1000 yhat A/m", "units": "A/m"}
limitingCases: ["A face normal parallel to M carries no equivalent surface current."]
pitfalls: ["The order M cross n matters; reversing it reverses circulation."]

title: Far-field magnetic dipole
latex: \mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r^3}[3(\mathbf m\cdot\hat{\mathbf r})\hat{\mathbf r}-\mathbf m]
plain: A localized current distribution has a leading magnetic dipole term.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "magnetic dipole moment", "unit": "A m^2", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "r", "meaning": "distance from source centre", "unit": "m", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "rhat", "meaning": "unit displacement", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "dipole field", "unit": "T", "kind": "vector"}]
conditions: ["r much larger than source extent; outside the source in vacuum."]

workedExample: {"inputs": "m=0.1 A m²; axial r=0.1 m", "steps": ["On axis B=mu0*2m/(4*pi*r³)."], "result": "B=20 microtesla", "units": "T"}
limitingCases: ["At the equator the field points opposite m with half the axial magnitude."]
pitfalls: ["The singular point-dipole field cannot describe the source interior."]

title: Dipole torque and energy
plain: A fixed permanent dipole tends to align with the applied field.
variables: [{"symbol": "tau", "meaning": "mechanical torque", "unit": "N m", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "fixed dipole moment", "unit": "A m^2", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "external field excluding self field", "unit": "T", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "U", "meaning": "orientation-dependent potential energy", "unit": "J", "kind": "scalar"}]

limitingCases: ["Aligned torque is zero although energy is minimal, not zero by necessity."]

title: Force on a fixed dipole
plain: The gradient of dipole potential gives force when its moment is fixed.
variables: [{"symbol": "F", "meaning": "force on dipole", "unit": "N", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "fixed moment", "unit": "A m^2", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "external induction", "unit": "T", "kind": "vector"}, {"symbol": "nabla", "meaning": "position gradient", "unit": "1/m", "kind": "operator"}]

pitfalls: ["Angle is measured from the normal, not from the surface plane."]

plain: An oriented quasistatic B–H loop gives magnetic work per sample volume for a completed cycle.

plain: A uniform ellipsoid gives a closed correction for reversible scalar susceptibility.

plain: Independent isotropically orientable moments respond linearly when thermal energy dominates alignment.
variables: [{"symbol": "mu0", "meaning": "vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant", "unit": "H/m", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "n", "meaning": "number density of moments", "unit": "1/m^3", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "mu", "meaning": "moment magnitude", "unit": "A m^2", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "kB", "meaning": "Boltzmann constant", "unit": "J/K", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "T", "meaning": "absolute temperature", "unit": "K", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "chi", "meaning": "small-field volume susceptibility", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}]

title: Period and frequency
plain: Frequency counts repeated cycles per elapsed time; period is the duration of one complete repetition. This definition presupposes a repeatable event and a declared clock, rather than assigning an oscillation to any object by naming it.
variables: [{"symbol": "f", "meaning": "ordinary frequency in cycles per second", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "T", "meaning": "period of one cycle", "unit": "s", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["T>0; stationary periodic signal; cycles counted consistently."]
derivation: ["Choose successive equivalent phase crossings.", "Divide the number of complete cycles by the elapsed time; for one cycle invert its duration."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"T_s": 0.002}, "steps": ["Invert 0.002 seconds."], "result": "500", "units": "Hz"}
limitingCases: ["As T grows without bound, f approaches zero."]
pitfalls: ["A transient or irregular record need not have one period."]

title: Ordinary versus angular frequency
plain: A full cycle is 2π radians. Ordinary frequency and angular frequency describe the same periodic evolution with different phase-counting conventions. The radian is a named dimensionless SI unit, but retaining rad in labels prevents factor-of-2π mistakes.
variables: [{"symbol": "ω", "meaning": "angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "f", "meaning": "ordinary frequency in cycles per second", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "π", "meaning": "circle constant, about 3.141592653589793", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "constant"}]
conditions: ["Sinusoidal phase or a specified phase-rate definition."]
derivation: ["One cycle increments phase by 2π.", "Differentiate phase 2πft with respect to time."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"f_Hz": 50}, "steps": ["Multiply 50 by 2π."], "result": "314.159", "units": "rad s⁻¹"}
limitingCases: ["Zero frequency gives zero angular frequency."]
pitfalls: ["Do not insert a frequency in Hz into an equation that expects rad/s."]

title: Instantaneous phase frequency
plain: For a resolved single-component signal, phase slope defines a local frequency. This is conditional on choosing a continuous phase representation and on adequate amplitude and signal quality. It is not a unique decomposition of an arbitrary multicomponent waveform.
variables: [{"symbol": "f", "meaning": "ordinary frequency in cycles per second", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "φ", "meaning": "continuous phase under stated unwrap convention", "unit": "rad", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "t", "meaning": "elapsed time", "unit": "s", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "π", "meaning": "circle constant, about 3.141592653589793", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "constant"}]
conditions: ["Unwrapped differentiable phase; amplitude not zero; phase model declared."]
derivation: ["Represent one component by amplitude times cosine of phase.", "Define frequency as cycles of phase accumulated per unit time."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"phase": "φ(t)=2π(100t+5t²)"}, "steps": ["Differentiate: dφ/dt=2π(100+10t).", "Evaluate at t=2 s."], "result": "120", "units": "Hz"}
limitingCases: ["Constant phase has zero local frequency."]
pitfalls: ["Phase at an amplitude zero can be undefined; differentiation amplifies noise."]

title: Undamped mass–spring natural frequency
plain: The free natural frequency follows from stiffness and inertia, not from the current drive. It is the frequency of one selected linearized coordinate under specified constraints. A real body generally supplies many coordinates and modes.
variables: [{"symbol": "ω₀", "meaning": "undamped natural angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "K", "meaning": "linear stiffness", "unit": "N m⁻¹", "kind": "coupling"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "mass", "unit": "kg", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["m>0; K>0; linear Hookean restoring force; no damping."]
derivation: ["Start with m x″+Kx=0.", "Insert x=A cos(ωt) and require K−mω²=0."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"K_N_per_m": 100, "m_kg": 1}, "steps": ["Take sqrt(100/1).", "Divide angular frequency by 2π to express Hz."], "result": "ω₀=10 rad/s; f₀≈1.59155 Hz", "units": "rad s⁻¹ and Hz"}
limitingCases: ["K→0 removes the restoring oscillation."]
pitfalls: ["Support stiffness and effective mass must match the same coordinate."]

title: Damped free oscillation
plain: A viscously damped oscillator rings with an exponential envelope and a shifted oscillation frequency. This describes the underdamped free motion; the frequency of the maximum forced displacement is a different quantity.
variables: [{"symbol": "ω_d", "meaning": "damped free angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "ω₀", "meaning": "undamped natural angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "γ", "meaning": "amplitude decay rate b/(2m)", "unit": "s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "b", "meaning": "viscous damping coefficient", "unit": "kg s⁻¹", "kind": "coupling"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "mass", "unit": "kg", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Linear viscous damping; 0≤γ<ω₀."]
derivation: ["Solve the characteristic polynomial r²+2γr+ω₀²=0.", "Its roots are −γ±iω_d; the real part sets decay and imaginary part sets oscillation."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"omega0_rad_s": 10, "gamma_per_s": 1}, "steps": ["Compute sqrt(100−1)."], "result": "9.949874", "units": "rad s⁻¹"}
limitingCases: ["At γ=0 recover ω₀; critical damping has no sinusoidal ringing."]
pitfalls: ["Do not continue the square root as a real oscillation above critical damping.", "Feynman I23 writes the damping coefficient as b/m; this atlas gamma is b/(2m), requiring an explicit factor-of-two translation."]

title: Quality factor in the weakly damped oscillator
plain: Quality factor compares stored energy with energy dissipated over an oscillation. For this linear viscous model the damping definition gives Q=ω₀/(2γ); the familiar energy-lost-per-cycle interpretation is most direct when damping is weak.
variables: [{"symbol": "Q", "meaning": "quality factor under the stated energy/linewidth convention", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "ω₀", "meaning": "undamped natural angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "γ", "meaning": "amplitude decay rate b/(2m)", "unit": "s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "mass", "unit": "kg", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "b", "meaning": "viscous damping coefficient", "unit": "kg s⁻¹", "kind": "coupling"}]
conditions: ["Positive viscous damping; energy/linewidth comparisons use weak damping."]
derivation: ["The displacement envelope decays as e^(−γt), so energy decays twice as fast.", "Compare the energy-loss timescale with the oscillation timescale."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"omega0_rad_s": 1000, "gamma_per_s": 5}, "steps": ["Divide 1000 by 10."], "result": "100", "units": "dimensionless"}
limitingCases: ["b→0 yields diverging Q in the lossless idealization."]
pitfalls: ["A high Q stores supplied energy; it is not energy creation.", "Feynman I23 writes the damping coefficient as b/m; this atlas gamma is b/(2m), requiring an explicit factor-of-two translation.", "Free ring-down amplitude decays at γ while energy decays at 2γ; loaded Q, internal Q and external-coupling Q are not interchangeable."]

title: Complex forced displacement response
plain: The displacement-to-force transfer function contains both gain and phase. The stated sign follows the e^(iωt) convention. It makes an experimentally useful prediction only when force and displacement channels, units, loading and calibration are specified.
variables: [{"symbol": "H", "meaning": "displacement/force frequency response", "unit": "m N⁻¹", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "K", "meaning": "linear stiffness", "unit": "N m⁻¹", "kind": "coupling"}, {"symbol": "m", "meaning": "mass", "unit": "kg", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "b", "meaning": "viscous damping coefficient", "unit": "kg s⁻¹", "kind": "coupling"}, {"symbol": "ω", "meaning": "angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "i", "meaning": "imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "constant"}]

limitingCases: ["At ω=0 recover static compliance 1/K."]
pitfalls: ["Changing phasor convention conjugates the imaginary sign, not the measurable prediction."]

title: Forced-displacement peak frequency
plain: For a flat force amplitude and frequency-independent viscous damping, the maximum displacement occurs below the undamped natural frequency. Other measured quantities, such as velocity, absorbed power or a microphone output, can peak elsewhere.
variables: [{"symbol": "ω_r", "meaning": "displacement-amplitude peak angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "ω₀", "meaning": "undamped natural angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "γ", "meaning": "amplitude decay rate b/(2m)", "unit": "s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}]

limitingCases: ["At zero damping this approaches ω₀; above the stated bound the interior displacement peak disappears."]
pitfalls: ["A spectral maximum does not automatically equal the isolated object natural mode.", "Feynman I23 writes the damping coefficient as b/m; this atlas gamma is b/(2m), requiring an explicit factor-of-two translation."]

title: Loaded resonance linewidth
plain: The linewidth relationship uses the half-power bandwidth of a single narrow resonance. Loaded Q includes energy loss through the measurement and drive ports as well as internal loss. A different amplitude threshold or a superposition of modes changes the inference.
variables: [{"symbol": "Q", "meaning": "quality factor under the stated energy/linewidth convention", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "f₀", "meaning": "centre frequency of the isolated narrow resonance", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "Δf", "meaning": "specified bandwidth or tone separation, as defined locally", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}]

limitingCases: ["Vanishing linewidth gives divergent ideal Q."]

title: Coupled normal-mode eigenproblem
plain: A coupled body has a family of mode shapes and eigenfrequencies. Positive mass and appropriate stiffness/boundary conditions determine the mathematical problem. A plotted shape alone does not specify the matrices, physical scale or material properties.

title: Nondispersive wave equation
plain: For a uniform one-dimensional nondispersive medium, sinusoidal plane waves satisfy a linear relation between angular frequency and spatial wave number. The medium speed belongs to that wave equation and is not automatically the vacuum speed of light.

limitingCases: ["At k=0 the chosen acoustic branch has ω=0."]

title: Phase and group velocity
plain: Phase speed follows constant phase; group speed follows the envelope of a narrow wave packet under suitable smooth dispersion. Neither expression alone proves a signal-front speed or licenses superluminal information transfer.

title: Fixed-end string modes
plain: A string fixed at both ends supports integer spatial half-wavelengths. This is a declared string model, not a formula that assigns a monument, sigil or arbitrary image its natural frequency.

plain: A separable pressure-wave model in a rigid rectangular cavity gives a modal family indexed by three nonnegative integers. Wall impedance, openings, obstacles and real geometry change this spectrum and its linewidths.

title: Continuous Fourier transform convention
plain: The transform resolves a time signal into complex frequency components under one explicit normalization. Displacement data produce transform units of metre-seconds. Generalized functions are needed for ideal infinite-duration pure tones.

title: Inverse Fourier reconstruction
plain: Under compatible hypotheses the inverse combines complex components to recover the signal. The frequency integral supplies inverse seconds, restoring the original signal units; phase is essential to the reconstruction.
variables: [{"symbol": "x", "meaning": "displacement", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "X(f)", "meaning": "continuous Fourier transform of x(t)", "unit": "m s", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "f", "meaning": "ordinary frequency in cycles per second", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "t", "meaning": "elapsed time", "unit": "s", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "π", "meaning": "circle constant, about 3.141592653589793", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "constant"}, {"symbol": "i", "meaning": "imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "constant"}]

title: Linear convolution theorem
plain: For a linear time-invariant channel, convolution in time corresponds to multiplication in frequency. The output spectrum includes the channel response, so a strong output line can come from propagation, sensor or electronics rather than the source alone.
variables: [{"symbol": "h(t)", "meaning": "time-domain LTI impulse-response kernel", "unit": "output/(input·s)", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "x(t)", "meaning": "input signal, here displacement for unit illustration", "unit": "m", "kind": "state"}, {"symbol": "*", "meaning": "convolution: (h*x)(t)=∫h(t−u)x(u)du, where u and t are time coordinates in seconds", "unit": "operator convention; includes integration over s", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "𝓕", "meaning": "Fourier transform with negative exponent −i2πft", "unit": "maps a signal unit to signal unit·s", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "H(f)", "meaning": "Fourier transform of the impulse response", "unit": "output/input", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "X(f)", "meaning": "Fourier transform of the input", "unit": "m s", "kind": "state"}, {"symbol": "f", "meaning": "ordinary transform frequency", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "coordinate"}]

limitingCases: ["H=0 suppresses every source component at that frequency."]
pitfalls: ["A transfer-function zero destroys information that naive division cannot restore."]

title: Causal Laplace transform and convergence
plain: The Laplace variable carries both decay/growth weighting and angular oscillation. Its region of convergence is part of the transform. A formal substitution s=iω does not establish that a Fourier transform exists on that boundary.
variables: [{"symbol": "X(s)", "meaning": "causal Laplace transform of displacement x(t)", "unit": "m s", "kind": "operator"}, {"symbol": "s", "meaning": "complex Laplace frequency σ+iω", "unit": "s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "σ", "meaning": "Laplace exponential growth/decay parameter", "unit": "s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "ω", "meaning": "angular frequency", "unit": "rad s⁻¹", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "x", "meaning": "displacement", "unit": "m", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "t", "meaning": "elapsed time", "unit": "s", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "i", "meaning": "imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "constant"}]

limitingCases: ["At s=0 recover total area 0.5 m·s."]

title: Finite discrete Fourier transform
plain: The DFT is an exact invertible change of coordinates for a finite sample vector under its chosen normalization. It is not, by itself, proof of the spectrum of the unsampled physical world.

title: DFT frequency grid
plain: The standard DFT grid spacing is reciprocal record duration. Zero padding provides additional interpolation points but does not create an independently longer measurement or separate arbitrarily close noisy components.
variables: [{"symbol": "f", "meaning": "ordinary frequency in cycles per second", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "k", "meaning": "DFT integer bin index", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "f_s", "meaning": "sampling rate", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "N", "meaning": "number of samples", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "Δf", "meaning": "specified bandwidth or tone separation, as defined locally", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "T_obs", "meaning": "observation duration", "unit": "s", "kind": "scalar"}]

title: Discrete-time alias equivalence
plain: Sampling identifies complex tones whose frequencies differ by an integer sampling rate. Real cosines add sign ambiguity. No later plot or machine-learning method can distinguish those aliases from the identical samples without additional assumptions or measurements.

title: Bandlimited sampling condition
plain: A strictly bandlimited signal can be reconstructed in the ideal sampling theorem when the sample rate exceeds twice its highest frequency. Equality is delicate: a sine exactly at Nyquist can vanish at every sample. Real hardware needs a transition band and analog filtering.
variables: [{"symbol": "f_max", "meaning": "highest absolute occupied signal frequency B, not an arbitrary oscillator carrier", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "f_s", "meaning": "uniform sampling rate", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "B", "meaning": "bandlimit used in the stated theorem hypothesis; equal to f_max", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["Ideal theorem: an L2 continuous-time signal has Fourier support in [−B,B] with B<f_s/2; infinitely many exact uniform samples and the associated ideal reconstruction are available. A finite record and real filter need extra error analysis."]

pitfalls: ["A high sample rate alone does not certify bandwidth, clock accuracy or sensor calibration."]

title: Periodic Hann analysis window
plain: Windowing reduces discontinuities in the assumed repeated record, trading spectral leakage against main-lobe width and changing amplitude normalization. The periodic N-denominator form differs from the symmetric N−1 form used in some applications.

conditions: ["N>1; explicitly periodic window for DFT analysis."]

pitfalls: ["Do not mix symmetric and periodic window calibration constants."]

title: Coherent window gain
plain: The mean window weight calibrates a bin-centred coherent tone under the declared transform convention. It is not the same normalization used for broadband noise power, which depends on the sum of squared weights.

pitfalls: ["For real tone amplitude, also account for the positive/negative-frequency split and DC/Nyquist exceptions."]

title: Two-sided windowed periodogram density
plain: Power spectral density records signal squared per hertz, rather than signal amplitude or a per-bin power. A one-sided real-data form doubles the positive interior bins, retaining separate DC and Nyquist treatment.

limitingCases: ["Zero samples produce zero PSD."]

title: DFT energy identity
plain: Parseval’s finite identity checks normalization by matching the squared norm in sample and DFT coordinates. It is a mathematical identity for this vector; converting it to physical energy still requires sample spacing, impedances and a calibrated channel model.

title: Short-time Fourier transform
plain: The STFT measures local spectral content under a chosen window and hop. It shows change across the record but trades temporal localization against frequency discrimination. A bright ridge is conditional on this representation and its calibration.

title: L2-normalized continuous wavelet transform
plain: Wavelet scale stretches a declared mother wavelet. Scale is not automatically hertz; converting it to frequency depends on the wavelet’s centre-frequency convention and sample period. Small sampled scales may alias even when the original input was properly sampled.

title: Floquet factorization of periodic linear dynamics
plain: A periodic linear differential equation admits a fundamental-matrix factorization under standard continuity conditions. The eigenvalues of its constant generator describe growth and phase modulo a drive-frequency convention. This is not a general claim that all periodically driven matter has a single frequency.

title: Optical frequency-comb tooth relation
plain: A stabilized comb links an integer sequence of optical modes to repetition and carrier-envelope-offset frequencies. Its utility requires mode-number identification, controlled offsets and a calibrated reference; the formula alone is not an accurate clock or range measurement.

conditions: ["Comb regime with identifiable mode index and defined offset/repetition references."]

title: Two-tone beating identity
plain: A pair of monaural tones has a rapid carrier factor and a slowly varying signed factor. The magnitude envelope repeats at the absolute tone separation. This algebra does not model dichotic binaural perception, EEG entrainment or clinical outcomes.

conditions: ["f_c=(f₁+f₂)/2; Δf=f₂−f₁; equal phases/amplitudes in this identity."]
derivation: ["Apply the sine-sum identity.", "Keep carrier frequency and tone separation as distinct observables."]

pitfalls: ["The signed cosine factor has frequency |Δf|/2; its absolute envelope has repetition rate |Δf|."]

title: Vacuum electromagnetic wavelength
plain: Frequency converts to wavelength through the propagation law of the declared channel. The exact vacuum speed applies to electromagnetic waves in vacuum. Acoustic frequency needs a sound speed, while a material dispersion relation can make phase and group wavelengths more complicated.

conditions: ["Vacuum electromagnetic plane wave; f>0."]

pitfalls: ["Do not use c₀/f for a sound wave in air or a body vibration."]

title: Quantum transition and photon energy
plain: A photon or an energy gap associated with a resonant quantum transition relates energy to temporal frequency through Planck’s constant. This does not identify the total energy of a classical acoustic wave from its frequency alone; occupation and amplitude also matter.

limitingCases: ["Zero frequency gives zero photon energy in this relation, not a nontrivial static photon oscillator."]
pitfalls: ["A classical oscillator has many energy levels/occupations; a high frequency alone is not a high total stored energy."]

title: Lorentzian field-coherence linewidth relation
plain: For a stationary exponentially decaying first-order field correlation, the spectrum is Lorentzian and its full-width-at-half-maximum is reciprocal π times the field-correlation time. Other line shapes or intensity-correlation definitions give different relations.

title: Fractional frequency deviation
plain: Fractional frequency compares an oscillator to a specified nominal/reference frequency. It is dimensionless and makes clock comparisons across very different carrier frequencies meaningful, while leaving reference calibration and correlations explicit.
variables: [{"symbol": "y", "meaning": "fractional frequency deviation", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "state"}, {"symbol": "ν", "meaning": "measured oscillator frequency", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "ν₀", "meaning": "nominal reference frequency", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}]

title: Non-overlapping Allan variance estimator
plain: Allan variance measures changes between adjacent averages rather than deviation from one global mean. The averaging time and noise class are essential. A stability statistic is not by itself a full systematic-uncertainty or accuracy evaluation.
variables: [{"symbol": "σ_y(τ)", "meaning": "Allan deviation at averaging time τ", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "τ", "meaning": "window centre or averaging time as declared locally", "unit": "s", "kind": "coordinate"}, {"symbol": "ȳ_i", "meaning": "mean fractional frequency in interval i of duration τ", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "state"}, {"symbol": "M", "meaning": "number of averaged-frequency observations", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}]
conditions: ["M≥2 adjacent non-overlapping interval averages of length τ; gaps/dead time and drift treatment stated."]
derivation: ["Compute adjacent averaged-frequency differences.", "Average their squares and divide by two."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"averages": [0, 1e-06, 0]}, "steps": ["Differences are +1e−6 and −1e−6.", "Squared sum divided by 4 is 5e−13."], "result": "variance=5e−13; deviation≈7.071e−7", "units": "dimensionless"}
limitingCases: ["A constant fractional offset has zero Allan variance."]

title: White-frequency averaging benchmark
plain: For white frequency noise and an appropriate measurement process, Allan deviation improves as averaging time to the minus one-half power. Drift, flicker floors, dead time and correlated noise prevent extrapolating this law indefinitely.
variables: [{"symbol": "σ_y(τ)", "meaning": "Allan deviation at averaging time τ", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "σ₁", "meaning": "white-frequency Allan deviation at τ=1 s", "unit": "dimensionless", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "τ", "meaning": "window centre or averaging time as declared locally", "unit": "s", "kind": "coordinate"}]
conditions: ["White frequency noise in the assessed averaging range; σ₁ refers to 1 s."]
derivation: ["Average independent fluctuations over more samples.", "Their variance falls inversely with averaging duration, so deviation falls as its square root."]
workedExample: {"inputs": {"sigma_at_1s": 1e-15, "tau_s": 100}, "steps": ["Divide 1e−15 by sqrt(100)."], "result": "1e−16", "units": "dimensionless"}

title: Weak-field gravitational clock shift
plain: Two otherwise comparable clocks at different gravitational potentials accumulate different proper times. Near Earth in a small static height interval, the higher clock runs faster by approximately gΔh/c₀². This is a conditional relativistic comparison, not motion changing an object’s intrinsic material constant.
variables: [{"symbol": "ν", "meaning": "measured oscillator frequency", "unit": "Hz", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "g", "meaning": "local gravitational acceleration", "unit": "m s⁻²", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "Δh", "meaning": "height difference under weak static-field approximation", "unit": "m", "kind": "scalar"}, {"symbol": "c₀", "meaning": "vacuum speed of light, exactly 299792458", "unit": "m s⁻¹", "kind": "constant"}]

plain: The unusually low-energy thorium-229 transition lies in the vacuum-ultraviolet optical range even though the participating states are nuclear. The word nuclear therefore does not by itself specify a gamma-ray frequency, clock performance or a deployed time standard.

title: First-order uncertainty propagation with covariance
plain: A differentiable map carries input covariance into output covariance through its Jacobian. Correlations can cancel or amplify uncertainty in ratios. This linearization must be checked when distributions, nonlinearity or denominator uncertainty are substantial.
variables: [{"symbol": "C_y", "meaning": "propagated output covariance matrix", "unit": "specified product of output units", "kind": "tensor"}, {"symbol": "J", "meaning": "Jacobian of derived quantities with respect to inputs", "unit": "output unit/input unit", "kind": "tensor"}, {"symbol": "C", "meaning": "input covariance matrix", "unit": "specified product of input units", "kind": "tensor"}]
conditions: ["Differentiable map near the estimate; small uncertainties; covariance and units declared."]
derivation: ["Linearize the map as δy≈Jδx.", "Take the covariance expectation while retaining cross terms."]
